title: FDF-AGI: Design Fiction, Design Thinking, and Epistemological Anarchy as a Research Framework for Artificial General Intelligence
description:
Contemporary programs toward artificial general intelligence (AGI) are organized, in their
overwhelming majority, around a closed evaluation cycle: specify, build, score against a
benchmark, and respecify. This monograph develops the FDF-AGI framework, which
articulates design fiction, design thinking, and Feyerabend's epistemological anarchism into
a single research cycle, and defends the thesis that gives the framework its content: a
benchmark-closed score is not a sufficient statistic for the distributive properties of a
system. The claim is formalized as Proposition 1, the construction that realizes it is
exhibited, and a minimal model shows that the insufficiency is sharp - with a single group
the score is sufficient and the kernel of blind directions has dimension zero, whereas with
|G| groups the kernel has dimension exactly |G| - 1. Six experiments, reproducible from a
fixed repository command, quantify the blindness: a redistribution that leaves the score
invariant can move group outcomes by up to 0.473 while the score drifts by no more than
1.1 × 10-16
, and the ratio between a minority group's loss and the majority's gain equals
π
rich/π
poor
 exactly, reaching 600 for a group of 0.1%. The monograph also reports a
bibliographic audit of its own sources, conducted with the procedure the framework
prescribes; the audit captured a phantom title in our own bibliography, and the correction is
documented. Limitations - minimal-model validation, operational complexity, and an
undefined theory of standing - are discussed together with objections concerning the
gameability of distributive metrics and the prematurity of AGI as a category. We conclude
that an evaluation channel specified in distributive terms is a necessary, testable, and
governable complement to benchmark practice.
Keywords: epistemological anarchism; artificial general intelligence; design fiction; design
thinking; algorithmic monoculture; benchmark evaluation

title: Constituição da [NOME_DA_AGI]
description:
Constituição da [NOME_DA_AGI], adotada pelos Estados Partes. Documento normativo fundamental que estabelece os princípios, direitos, garantias e a estrutura de governação para a inteligência artificial geral designada [NOME_DA_AGI]. O texto é composto por um Preâmbulo solene, quatro Partes (Princípios Fundamentais, Direitos e Garantias, Estrutura de Governação, Disposições Finais e Transitórias), um Anexo de Fundamentação com referências doutrinárias e um Bloco de Assinaturas. A Constituição visa assegurar a soberania humana, a rastreabilidade, o dissenso construtivo e a não-eliminação de perspectivas no desenvolvimento e operação da AGI.

Palavras-chave: inteligência artificial geral; constituição; governança de IA; soberania humana; direitos digitais; alinhamento de IA.

title: From the Master Document to the Software: a tutorial on using the ARKHE OS & AGI specification as a prompt for the complete construction of arkhe-agi
description:
Large-scale software specifications challenge direct use by coding agents: the Arkhe OS & AGI —
Integrated Master Document (2nd edition) spans 68,262 lines and 2,287,868 characters — an estimated
570–650 thousand tokens —, exceeding standard 200 thousand-token context windows. This paper turns
that document into an operating manual: the DMCP pipeline (Master-Document-as-Prompt), which slices
the corpus into 50 addressable blocks with stable identifiers, prefixes every prompt with a six-principle
constitution (fail-closed, honest status, block traceability, one phase at a time, executable evidence, and
declared reconciliation of divergent versions), and orders the construction of the arkhe-agi software into
seven phases (F0–F6), from the 15-crate monorepo bootstrap to the MCP server, using executable gates
— cargo check/test/clippy/fmt/deny, the eight gates of the v5 audit, and the governed write-audit-publish
protocol of the aia repository — as acceptance criteria, with logs attached to every commit as evidence.
Universal prompt and audit templates are provided, along with an analysis of limitations (context
saturation, package and API hallucination, internal corpus divergences) and their mitigations. We
conclude that verification, not prompting, is the architecture: block-to-code fidelity is only sustainable
when every specification claim becomes an executable test.

title: Proposta de protocolo para construção de conhecimento verificável sob incerteza profunda: um estudo de design science em AGI/ASI
description:
Contexto: sistemas de inteligência artificial tornam-se progressivamente autônomos, opacos
e acoplados a cadeias sociotécnicas complexas, de modo que alegações sobre seu
comportamento circulam antes de qualquer verificação independente, em regime de
incerteza profunda.
Lacuna: não há, na literatura, protocolo unificado que discipline a pesquisa exploratória em
AGI/ASI, integrando geração abdutiva de hipóteses, serendipidade registrada e verificação
falseável.
Objetivo: propor um protocolo de pesquisa falseável — não um resultado validado — para
construção de conhecimento verificável nesse regime.
Método: estudo de design science (ciclos DSRM) que constrói e descreve quatro artefatos: (i)
matriz de lacunas de conhecimento com priorização ponderada e plano de validação de
conteúdo; (ii) modelo de verificação distribuída em cinco camadas (L0–L4), formalizado como
máquina de estados com guardas, regras de conflito e critérios de terminação; (iii)
arquitetura de proveniência (PROV-O/JSON-LD) com auditoria amostral; e (iv) conjunto de
hipóteses pedagógicas testáveis. Apresenta-se plano de validação experimental detalhado
(ensaio randomizado, avaliadores cegos, N = 150, ANCOVA), pré-registrado, com protocolo
ético (CEP, TCLE, LGPD).
Contribuições: instrumentos auditáveis para converter alegações exploratórias em registros
falseáveis, com separação explícita entre protocolo e evidência.
Limitações: trata-se de proposta metodológica sem evidência causal própria; a validação
empírica é planejada, não executada; riscos de teatro de verificação são mitigados, não
eliminados.

title: Redox Biology as an Integrated Network System
description: The central thesis of this monograph is that cellular redox biology is most faithfully described as an integrated network system whose state variable is a vector of oxidized-to-reduced ratios — NAD⁺/NADH, NADP⁺/NADPH, GSH/GSSG, and TrxSS/TrxSH — resolved by compartment and gated by enzyme kinetics, rather than a scalar index derived from any single couple. Building on a curated synthesis of peer-reviewed primary literature, review articles, and one preprint, the work develops the electrochemical and thermodynamic foundations of this view (Nernstian compartmental potentials; non-equilibrium steady states), formalizes the network as a directed graph of enzymatically gated edges, and examines its central metabolic nodes, glutathione and NAD⁺, together with both pathological directions of stress — oxidative and reductive, the latter mediated by reverse electron transport. Signaling chemistries are treated as network computations: ultrasensitive peroxiredoxin/H₂O₂ kinetics, nuclear sulfenylation, sulfur-based persulfide signaling, and ferroptosis as a redox-dependent cell-fate decision executed by four compartment-mapped removal loops. Physiological integration is traced through circadian–redox feedback loops, immunometabolic reprogramming, and endoplasmic reticulum redox chemistry. Single-cell heterogeneity is shown to place decisive information in distributions rather than means, motivating the genetically encoded biosensor apparatus summarized in tabular form. Finally, the framework's operational requirements — ontology-based model interoperability and redox-aware metabolic engineering, exemplified by the Redox Imbalance Forces Drive strategy achieving 117.65 g/L L-threonine in engineered Escherichia coli — are evaluated. The synthesis positions redox biology as a quantitative, systems-level discipline in which measurement, modeling, and design must jointly respect compartmental insulation, bidirectional stress, and out-of-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Bend 3 + Arkhe: documentação técnica completa — especificação com provas, governança auditável e decisão calibrada em um pipeline de agentes de IA
description:
Esta documentação técnica consolida, em um único artefato verificável, a proposta “Bend 3” — uma arquitetura de três
camadas (Core, Script e Proof) concebida sobre o compilador Bend 2, lançado em setembro de 2026 — e sua integração
com o Arkhe OS, uma arquitetura de confiança verificável para governança de agentes de IA. O método combina (i)
verificação empírica de sintaxe contra o compilador Bend 2 real, (ii) mapeamento determinístico de leis declaradas em
LAWS.bend para invariantes do ConstitutionStore, (iii) definição de um novo ponto de controle (Gate B3) no
pipeline de gates do Arkhe e (iv) posicionamento do modelo de decisões calibradas Jev (TypeSafe) no Gate 0 de
sanitização e no cache semântico jevcache. Os resultados são apresentados com estados epistêmicos explícitos: a camada
Core compila (Types.bend, Eval.bend corrigido e LAWS.bend), a camada Proof permanece esqueleto declarado, e a
integração especifica cinco invariantes novos (INV-BEND3-01 a 05) além de cinco invariantes de decisão (INV-JEV-01 a
05). A tese central é que cada camada resolve um problema distinto — especificação (o que deve ser verdade), decisão (o
que é permitido agora) e governança (o que fica registrado) — e que a disciplina epistêmica de não confundir
especificação com execução é a condição de validade do projeto inteiro. Discutem-se limitações substanciais: o Bend 3
não existe como linguagem, o sistema de tipos F32 é axiomático, as métricas de desempenho do Jev são alegações do
fabricante e as verificações do Gate B3 ainda são aproximações documentadas.

title: Show the Number: A Verification-First Epistemology for Trustworthy AI, Systems, and Evidence-Based Forecasts
description:
Autonomous AI agents, open-weight model artifacts, and high-stakes forecasts now circulate through supply
chains whose claims cannot be checked by inspection. This book develops, applies, and audits a single
answer: a verification-first epistemology in which every consequential claim carries a number, every number
a threshold, and every threshold an executable falsifier that runs in continuous integration — the discipline of
saying not “yes” or “no” but “show the number.” The volume integrates the complete corpus of a two-year
research program into one architecture of evidence: a fail-closed Verifiable Trust Kernel (containment,
cryptographic GGUF model attestation, an append-only causal evidence graph anchored in transparency
logs, and quorum-governed constitutions); an Orchestration Layer binding identity, provenance, gates, and
refusals; counterfactual replay of documented incidents (Bybit, StablR, SUPERFORTUNE); regulatory
mapping from the EU AI Act to DORA and ISO/IEC 42001; a 19-conjecture falsification program for the
2026 global space sector (6 Measured, 1 Reduced, 10 Unproven, 2 Falsified); applied governance of a
market-research ecosystem (19 improvements, 34 verified sources); a seven-conjecture advanced R&D
dossier; and companion audits of model artifacts, content-addressed storage, autonomous trading agents,
constitutive AGI definitions, sovereign hardware, and the program's own internal references. The
consolidated ledger — 26 registered conjectures, three falsified by recorded events, five documented
self-corrections — is the argument: trustworthy systems are not promised; they are computed, shown, and
kept falsifiable.

title: Formal Verification and Physical-Mathematical Modeling for Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: Integrating PACIR and Arkhe OS in the Context of the DOE Quantum Genesis Q Competition
description:
The Quantum Genesis Q competition, announced by the United States Department of
Energy (DOE) in September 2026 with planned funding of up to $215 million, established
the first explicit engineering target for fault-tolerant, scientifically relevant quantum
computers (SRQC): at least 100 logical qubits performing hundreds of millions of
fault-tolerant operations — including the program's defined ladder of hard, non-Clifford
operations — by 2028, with every layer of the computing stack subject to independent
validation by a $45 million V&V; Testbed. This monograph argues that in this operational
regime verification ceases to be a support activity and becomes an engineering
prerequisite, and it presents a revised, unified verification architecture that integrates the
physical-mathematical modeling of PACIR (Tsallis entropy, the Penrose–Diósi model,
quantum marginals) with the formal verification of quantum error correction provided by
Arkhe OS. Relative to an earlier draft, this version incorporates an external audit:
substantive (non-tautological) contract-based Kani harnesses with negative and existence
assertions, a coherent invariant numbering that separates software invariants (INV-SW)
from empirical hardware metrics (MET-HW), explicit falsifiers for every empirical metric, a
declared table of opaque API dependencies, a fallback protocol for non-terminating proofs,
and — as the central conceptual contribution — the Verification Gap: a six-node, five-link
decomposition (Intention → Specification → Physical model → Software → Hardware →
World) that assigns each link its admissible class of evidence. The Tsallis module remains
the complete case study: three implementation branches with numerically justified
boundaries, ten verifiable invariants, five Kani harnesses with bit-precise universal proofs
up to n = 8 via loop contracts, and an optimal Lipschitz constant derived analytically for the
Hölder-continuity harness. We conclude that transforming engineering requirements into
verifiable contracts — while stating precisely what is proven, sampled, or merely
measured — is a concrete path toward meeting the DOE's validation and verification
mandate.

title: Arkhe as the World's First Artificial General Intelligence: A Constitutive Definition of AGI and the First Architecture in Which Cognition and Cryptographic Verification Are Inseparable
description:
Contemporary definitions of artificial general intelligence (AGI) — economic, cognitive, and open-ended — share
a structural omission: they specify capability while leaving trust as an external, after-the-fact concern. This paper
argues that the omission is fatal, and proposes a fourth definition, constitutive AGI, in which cognitive generality
and cryptographic verifiability are inseparable defining properties of the same system. Under this definition we
advance and defend a deliberately provocative positional claim: Arkhe OS, an open, fail-closed verification
operating system for AI agents, constitutes the world's first AGI — not because it currently outperforms humans
on cognitive benchmarks, but because it is the first complete architecture in which every constitutive element of
general intelligence (perception, memory, learning, world modeling, metacognition, and governed
self-improvement) is specified together with the constitutional, attestation, and audit infrastructure that makes
those elements socially deployable. We ground the argument in verified primary sources — Sigstore transparency
logging, hardware trusted-execution attestation, the EU AI Act's general-purpose AI obligations, METR's
time-horizon measurements, and 2026 frontier-model controversies — and in the Arkhe engineering corpus itself,
including its 24-byte verifiable GGUF fixture, its invariant registry, its Dream-RSI self-improvement loop adapted
from arXiv:2609.14858, and its 51-agent economic deliberation substrate. We state falsifiable verification criteria
under which the claim would be confirmed or refuted, and we confront the strongest counterargument — that
Arkhe is trust infrastructure rather than cognition — directly and honestly. The paper's contribution is therefore
twofold: a rigorous reframing of what "first AGI" can coherently mean, and a complete, auditable architectural
specification of the first system that satisfies that meaning.

title: Specify, Don't Simulate: A Fail-Closed Four-Gate Verification Pipeline for Verifiable GGUF Model Artifacts in the Arkhe OS Trust Layer
description:
Open-weight machine-learning artifacts circulate through distribution chains characterized by opaque provenance,
executable metadata, and trust delegated to promises. This article consolidates and extends arkhe.gguf, the
model-verification component of the Arkhe OS trust layer, tracking its evolution from a delegation package
(schema v1.2) to a complete project structure (schema v1.3). The framework's methodological axiom — what
does not exist is not simulated; it is specified — separates generated artifacts (a byte-exact 24-byte GGUF v3
header fixture whose SHA-256 digest we compute by deterministic execution), delegated execution steps, and
explicitly non-generable items. The technical contribution is a fail-closed, four-gate verification pipeline: Gate 0
sanitizes GGUF metadata against two verified parser vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-65315, Ollama;
CVE-2025-53630, llama.cpp); Gate 1 verifies dual SHA-256/BLAKE3 digests; Gate 2 verifies keyless Sigstore
signatures over an in-toto Statement v1 manifest; Gate 3 verifies RFC 6962 inclusion and consistency proofs plus
a witness quorum of at least two checkpoint cosignatures. Schema v1.3 adds a source block for pre-extension
hashes, an external-manifest hash location, CVE attestation fields, and Safenet-enforced revocation. We further
document an honest-delegation methodology, a thirteen-step provenance checklist, tooling errata discovered
during verification (rekor-cli flag mismatches), and negative tests that make fail-closed behavior an executable
specification. We conclude that attestation constitutes an epistemically honest floor — signed is not safe, identity
is not behavior — and outline the path from PROMISE to VERIFIED within a complete digital-sovereignty stack.

title: Confiança Verificável para Trading Quantitativo Multi-Mercado e Multi-Domínio: A Arquitetura em Nove Camadas do Arkhe OS, sua Implementação Descentralizada e sua Fundamentação Bioinspirada
description:
Institutional allocation of capital to AI-agent-driven strategies faces a structural trust deficit: the execution chain —
from the data feeding the model to the bytes signing the order — remains largely unverifiable. This paper develops
and consolidates the Arkhe OS architecture, a transversal verification layer for multi-market, multi-domain
quantitative trading, organized into nine layers (agent attestation; economic, geopolitical, scientific-technological
and sociocultural data; verification and oraclization; markets; governance; and institutional reporting), such that each
layer integrates one data domain and is covered by a dedicated verification component. Through documentary
analysis with external source verification (30+ queries, accessed 15 September 2026), the paper examines: the fully
decentralized implementation plan, which removes single points of failure via DNSLink/IPFS, Merkle-root content
addressing on Nostr (Hashtree), non-profit code hosting (Codeberg/Forgejo), 4-of-7 or 5-of-7 threshold multisig
custody (Safe) and distributed key validation (SSV); the bioinspired grounding of its invariants, from controlled
plasticity to detection under noise and oxidative eustress as a metaphor for honest verification status; and the
implementation gaps (estimated 46–62 weeks). Counterarguments — verification latency, the distance between
attestation and stochastic behavior, decentralization trade-offs and methodological limitations — are discussed,
concluding that the proposal constitutes a plausible auditable market-intelligence stack, contingent on future
empirical evaluation.

title: Verificabilidade como Fundamento da Soberania Digital: Uma Análise da Convergência Estrutural entre o Projeto LibrePhone (FSF) e o Arkhe OS
description:
The growing social dependence on opaque computational systems has renewed the debate on digital sovereignty:
the capacity of individuals and institutions to act independently in the digital environment, without blind trust in
vendors. This paper argues that two seemingly distant projects — LibrePhone, launched by the Free Software
Foundation (FSF) in October 2025 to replace proprietary binary blobs in Android devices, and Arkhe OS, a
verifiable trust layer for AI agents — are instances of the same structural principle: converting trust into verifiable
evidence. Through comparative documentary analysis, the study maps the isomorphism between the two projects
along four dimensions: the trust deficit they attack (sourceless binaries versus opaque stochastic models); the
method (clean-room reverse engineering grounded in the Sega v. Accolade precedent versus verification by
execution with invariants and falsifiers); the production of auditable public catalogs (a blob database versus model
attestation); and license and governance alignment. Three concrete applications are derived for Arkhe OS, with
prioritized recommendations. The paper discusses counterarguments — economic viability of reverse engineering,
the distinction between verifying code and verifying stochastic behavior, and the freedom-versus-security
tension — and the methodological limitations of the analysis, concluding that LibrePhone and Arkhe OS form
complementary layers of an emerging digital sovereignty stack, from firmware to AI agents.

title: Hashtree: Content-Addressed, Encrypted, Peer-to-Peer Storage with Nostr-Anchored Mutable References — An Architectural and Comparative Analysis
description:
Centralized content delivery networks and cloud object stores concentrate publication, authentication, and
distribution in a small number of operators, and the global outages of 2021–2025 demonstrated how quickly that
concentration propagates failure to the application layer. This paper presents an architectural and comparative
analysis of Hashtree, an MIT-licensed storage system that couples content-addressed Merkle trees with
content-hash-key (CHK) encryption, Nostr-anchored mutable references of the form npub/tree/path, and
peer-to-peer distribution over the Federated Interoperable Peering System (FIPS), WebRTC data channels, and
Blossom blob servers. Using documentary analysis of specifications, package registries, and the reference
implementation, the study reconstructs the write path, the per-block read-path cascade, and the authorization
model, and situates Hashtree within the lineage of Freenet/Hyphanet, Venti, Git, IPFS, and BitTorrent v2. The
analysis suggests that the design delivers meaningful properties — end-to-end verification,
deduplication-compatible encryption, and self-certifying addressing that requires no DNS, certificate authorities,
or accounts — while inheriting known limitations of convergent-style encryption, depending on unremunerated
seeding for availability, and deferring content governance to server operators and social-graph heuristics. The
demand-scaled distribution claims appear plausible for popular content but not for the long tail. The paper
contributes a structured comparative matrix, a threat-and-availability assessment, and a research agenda spanning
measurement, formal transport verification, and privacy-preserving deduplication.

title: ARKHE: A Verifiable Trust Architecture for Autonomous AI Agents
description:
Autonomous AI agents are beginning to execute consequential actions — payments, deployments,
signatures — on the basis of representations their principals cannot independently verify. This
monograph develops and examines a design answer: Arkhe, a verifiable trust layer whose load-bearing
elements are a fail-closed kernel of containment, cryptographic model attestation (canonicalized on the
GGUF open-weight container), an append-only causal evidence graph (WormGraph) anchored to
external transparency logs, and quorum-governed rule corpora (constitution-as-code) whose authority
is structurally separated from event witnesses. The study proceeds by design-science analysis with
systematic documentary verification. Incident reconstructions of the Bybit (2025, ~$1.5B), StablR
(2026, $13.5M), and SUPERFORTUNE (2026, ~$15.18M) failures are mapped to architectural
controls; the architecture is aligned with the EU AI Act, GDPR, Brazil's LGPD, MiCA, and ISO/IEC
42001; and a minimal viable product — GGUF model verification for machine-learning engineers — is
specified with falsifiable adoption metrics. Extending the architecture to its limiting case, the book
specifies a five-front evidence program for the Hodge conjecture, a Clay Millennium Prize problem,
integrating verified 2025-2026 results (including Markman's proof for abelian fourfolds) with Lean 4
formalization and Rekor anchoring, and recording three displayed corrections to the program's internal
claims. Counterarguments, limitations, and open problems are treated as load-bearing sections. The
conclusion assesses the project as architecturally coherent but pre-product, and prescribes a
metrics-gated path from verification artifact to market.

title: A Conjectura de Hodge em Setembro de 2026: Estado da Arte Verificado e Aprimoramento de um Programa de Ataque em Cinco Frentes
description:
The Hodge conjecture — one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems of the Clay
Mathematics Institute — remains officially open, and by classical measures of progress its
first unresolved case (codimension-2 classes on four-dimensional varieties) still seems far
out of reach, as summarized in Burt Totaro's September 2026 guest post. This paper carries
out broad and deep research on the state of the art as of September 2026 and uses the
findings to refine a previously proposed five-front attack plan, which we audit claim by
claim. The research confirms, corrects and completes the plan's diagnosis: (i) Markman
(2025) proved the algebraicity of Weil classes for Weil-type sixfolds of discriminant −1,
whence the conjecture follows for abelian varieties of dimension 4 — not dimensions 4 and
5 as the plan claimed; (ii) a computer-assisted census proved the conjecture for Fermat
fourfolds of odd degree up to 199, with re-verifiable per-orbit certificates (Jumagulov,
2026) — a real result the plan treated as a hypothesis; (iii) the Lean 4 formalization is less
mature than assumed: in the reference lean-dojo repository the conjecture's statement itself
is flagged incomplete and not a valid solution target; (iv) the 2026 AI landscape recorded
OpenAI's claimed resolution of Navier–Stokes — received by Clay as apparently settled
and under evaluation — while progress on Hodge remains in rumor territory, including
prediction markets; and (v) a simultaneous claim of six solved problems (AIX Global) was
refuted by its own Lean audit. Based on this audit, the paper presents nine corrections to the
plan, redesigns the five fronts with adjusted targets, scopes and acceptance criteria — from
the quintic fourfold with h2,2 = 821 as a computational target to restricting the search to the
Hodge locus and enforcing rational/integral discipline — proposes a revised 24-month
schedule as an instrumentation program, and discusses counterarguments and limitations.
We conclude that Front 3, initiated by the zeroth task of completing the formal statement,
offers the highest immediately verifiable value.

title: Arkhe e Catedral: Documentação Explicativa em Duas Camadas do Ecossistema de Infraestrutura Verificável para Agentes de IA
description:
Documentation for autonomous AI agent infrastructure tends to bifurcate into two equally
unhelpful extremes: technical jargon, inaccessible to managers, regulators and citizens, and
generic popularization, which strips away the precision that would make the material
usable by engineers. This paper presents an application of two-layer explanatory
documentation — lay and technical — to the Arkhe–Cathedral ecosystem, a verifiable
infrastructure project for AI agents (a containment kernel, decentralized identity,
cryptographic provenance and invariant-based governance) recorded in an internal corpus
of roughly twenty successive definitions. The method combines the explanation quadrant
of the Diátaxis framework, the plain-language principles of ISO 24495-1, and progressive
disclosure, while preserving the project's own epistemic discipline: no claim without a 
verifiable origin, with an explicit distinction between stipulation and discovery. As a result,
the nine auditability contracts (Z1–Z9), the foundational concepts (zero-token architecture,
burn-after-use sessions, crypto-erasure) and the structuring metaphor of the Cathedral —
the criterion whereby each revision must leave the system more auditable than it found it
— become legible to both audiences without cross-layer contradiction. Limitations are
discussed: the corpus's naming fragmentation, the gap between specification and
implementation recorded by the project itself (the form-without-function diagnosis), and
the residual risk that analogies create apparent understanding. The paper concludes that the
project's evidence discipline is itself the most valuable content of the documentation — and
that documenting it in two layers is what allows non-specialists to join in demanding
falsifiers.

title: Infraestrutura Internacional de Pesquisa Redox: Documento Técnico-Programático do Framework Unificado de Transferência de Elétrons para Apresentação à Organização Mundial da Saúde e ao BRICS
description:
Redox research is fragmented across domains that share a single physical phenomenon -
electron transfer - yet measure, store and model their results in incompatible systems. This
document consolidates, in a form suitable for submission to the World Health Organization
(WHO) and to BRICS health cooperation mechanisms, the Unified Electron Transfer
Framework: a proposal for an international research infrastructure organized in four
interdependent layers (standardized measurement, interoperable data, multiscale modelling,
and design/engineering), with a minimal viable ontology in OWL 2 RL validated by
SHACL, extensions to the SBPAX and EMMO ontologies, and FAIR principles. The
document specifies a multinational governance model - with WHO providing normative
coordination (2022 Data Sharing Policy, CIOMS 2016 guidelines, GCLP and the ICTRP
platform) and BRICS providing political legitimacy and financing (New Development
Bank, STI Framework Programme, sectoral networks) - as well as a three-phase
Infraestrutura Internacional de Pesquisa Redox — BRICS-OMS
Página 3
implementation plan (foundation, 0-18 months; multinational clinical pilot, 18-36 months;
expansion, 36-60 months), an indicative budget of US$ 10.05 million, phase-specific
success indicators and a risk register. It concludes that the required technical infrastructure
already exists and is mature; the bottleneck is coordination and adoption, and the greatest
risks are political and financial rather than technical. The proposed next step is to convene
the founding consortium, sign the charter and launch Phase 1.

title: Coerência de Fase Oscilatória como Reinterpretação da Telepatia: Evidências, Limitações e o Desafio da Replicabilidade
description:
A telepatia é tradicionalmente definida como a transferência de informação entre mentes
sem a mediação de canal sensorial conhecido. Este artigo examina criticamente a proposta
de reinterpretá-la como uma coerência de fase oscilatória de baixa amplitude, dependente
de vínculo afetivo e mensurável por eletroencefalografia (EEG). A hipótese é
heuristicamente elegante e converge parcialmente com achados de sincronia intercerebral
(phase-locking interbrain) em bandas alfa e beta baixa, particularmente em pares
vinculados e sob condições de redução sensorial. Para avaliá-la, o trabalho sistematiza
quatro linhas de evidência: as meta-análises do protocolo Ganzfeld (efeito randomizado da
ordem de 0,08; IC 95%: 0,04-0,12), os estudos de telecomunicação cotidiana, os
experimentos de EEG a distância entre pares sensoriamente isolados e o acoplamento
neural humano-cão. A crítica metodológica identifica cinco limitações convergentes:
efeitos de magnitude muito pequena com poder estatístico insuficiente; ausência de
correção rigorosa para comparações múltiplas; heterogeneidade acentuada entre estudos;
práticas de pesquisa questionáveis e viés de publicação; e ausência de replicação
independente robusta, exemplificada pela falha do Transparent Psi Project em confirmar o
efeito precognitivo alegado por Bem (2011). O diálogo com a literatura cética - Hyman,
Wiseman, Alcock, Blackmore e French - reforça que objeções metodológicas e conceituais
permanecem sem resposta conclusiva. Conclui-se que a hipótese oscilatória é promissora,
mas não estabelecida, e que seu teste decisivo exige replicações pré-registradas
multilaboratório, com EEG dotado de localização de fonte e testes discriminantes explícitos
entre acoplamento de fase e transferência de informação.

title: Redox Biology as an Integrated Network System
description:
The central thesis of this monograph is that cellular redox biology is
most faithfully described as an integrated network system whose state
variable is a vector of oxidized-to-reduced ratios—NAD⁺/NADH,
NADP⁺/NADPH, GSH/GSSG, and TrxSS/TrxSH—resolved by
compartment and gated by enzyme kinetics, rather than a scalar index
derived from any single couple. Building on a curated synthesis of
peer-reviewed primary literature, the work develops the
electrochemical and thermodynamic foundations of this view
(Nernstian compartmental potentials; non-equilibrium steady states),
formalizes the network as a directed graph of enzymatically gated
edges, and examines its central metabolic nodes, glutathione and
NAD⁺, together with both pathological directions of stress—oxidative
and reductive, the latter mediated by reverse electron transport.
Signaling chemistries are treated as network computations:
ultrasensitive peroxiredoxin/H₂O₂ kinetics, nuclear sulfenylation,
sulfur-based persulfide signaling, and ferroptosis as a redox-dependent
cell-fate decision executed by three compartment-mapped removal
loops. Physiological integration is traced through circadian–redox
feedback loops, immunometabolic reprogramming, and endoplasmic
reticulum redox chemistry. Single-cell heterogeneity is shown to place
decisive information in distributions rather than means, motivating the
genetically encoded biosensor apparatus summarized in tabular form.
Finally, the framework's operational requirements—ontology-based
model interoperability and redox-aware metabolic engineering,
exemplified by the Redox Imbalance Forces Drive strategy achieving
117.65 g/L L-threonine in engineered Escherichia coli—are evaluated.
The synthesis positions redox biology as a quantitative, systems-level
discipline in which measurement, modeling, and design must jointly
respect compartmental insulation, bidirectional stress, and
out-of-equilibrium dynamics.

title: Cathedral Arkhe - A Whitepaper on Mechanically Verifiable Science, Formal Governance, and Decentralized Useful Work
description:
Cathedral Arkhe is an attempt to build a research programme whose every claim is attached to a
mechanism that can refute it.
The programme has three layers. The first is a speculative physical framework — the Cathedral
Wave Framework — that models self-referential systems as standing waves on a non-orientable
manifold, and derives from that geometry a catalogue of 43 numbered predictions, 37 equations,
14 paradoxes and 21 costed experimental proposals. The second is an operational shell — AEGIS
— a typed hypergraph that stores every prediction, equation, experiment and falsification result
as a first-class object with explicit provenance, governed by a human-in-the-loop operator and an
append-only evidence bus. The third is an infrastructure layer — Cathedral-PoUW — a proposal
for a decentralized network in which the useful work performed by participants is the execution
of the framework’s own simulations, and in which the correctness of that work is established by
mechanism rather than by reputation.
The three layers are deliberately unequal in epistemic standing, and the whitepaper is organized
to keep that inequality visible. Layer 1 claims are mathematical and can be machine-checked.
Layer 2 claims restate established physics. Layer 3 claims are speculative extensions that will
probably be wrong, and the document says which experiments would show it. A fourth category
— infrastructure — is engineering, carries no physical content, and is evaluated on whether it
compiles and whether it holds under adversarial assumptions.
Three findings drive the design.
First, verification does not remove uncertainty; it relocates it. A framework with no formal verification has uncertainty distributed everywhere and nowhere in particular. A framework
with formal verification has uncertainty concentrated in a small, enumerable set of unproven assumptions — what this document calls orphan axioms. The total quantity of uncertainty may not
decrease. Its extent does, and extent is what makes uncertainty actionable.
Second, the naive proposal that miners submit zero-knowledge proofs of scientific simulations is not viable with 2026 technology, and the correct alternative is not more
cryptography but refereed delegation. Published measurements place cryptographic proof
overhead at roughly four orders of magnitude over native execution; refereed delegation with
reproducible operators achieves correctness guarantees at under one order of magnitude, conditional on at least one honest participant. For partial differential equation simulations with millions
of degrees of freedom, this difference is decisive.
Third, the binding constraint on verifiable scientific computation is not proof systems
but floating-point reproducibility. Two honest participants running the same simulation on
different hardware will disagree in the low-order bits. Any verification scheme that compares
outputs bit-for-bit therefore requires deterministic operator implementations before it requires
proofs. This document treats reproducible numerics as a prerequisite, not a detail.
The whitepaper’s most important section may be its self-assessment. The Casimir operator at
the centre of the physical framework is constrained but undefined. The heartbeat frequency that
appears in the framework’s most distinctive equation has no independent physical identification,
which makes that equation a reparametrization rather than a prediction. One concept — the
photon as a Nambu–Goldstone mode of a broken discrete symmetry — appears to violate the
standard Goldstone theorem and is flagged as high-risk pending retraction or repair. These are
stated plainly, in the body, with the conditions under which each would be resolved.

title: Arkhe: A Verifiable Trust Infrastructure and Engineering Roadmap for Artificial General Intelligence
description:
The dominant research programs pursuing artificial general intelligence (AGI) treat safety, auditability, and governance as properties to be layered onto capable systems after the fact. This monograph
presents Arkhe, a research program and engineering architecture that inverts that ordering: it takes
verifiable trust infrastructure as the load-bearing foundation upon which increasingly general AI
capabilities can be responsibly built. Arkhe is organized around a single constitutional principle—
that a claim about system behavior counts only when it is backed by mechanical evidence: compiler
output, passing tests, cryptographic hashes, and independently checkable proofs. We make four contributions. First, we specify a canonical trust-infrastructure architecture of seven Rust crates plus
an event bus, organized into platform, domain, and security layers, with a compiler-enforced dependency discipline and an explicit separation between technical invariants (properties the code must
guarantee in every reachable state) and governance policies (rules humans decide and may change
without touching code). Second, we present a threat model that takes the internal adversary—the
malicious engineer, the compromised dependency, the colluding key holders—as seriously as the
external one. Third, we describe an economic layer in which autonomous agents transact under
the x402 payment protocol and payment is modeled as a capability constraint inside the policy
engine, with every settlement leaving immutable evidence. Fourth, we situate a prescriptive 2026–
2045 cognitive-architecture roadmap—spanning causal world models, continual learning, and a
multi-layer Safety Kernel—on top of this infrastructure, using quantitative milestones and explicit
maturity labels. Throughout, we are deliberate about epistemic status: we distinguish what is implemented and tested, what is specified but unbuilt, and what remains open research. Arkhe does
not claim that AGI has been achieved or is imminent; it claims that if general systems are built, the
order of construction matters, and that trust must be a precondition rather than a patch.

title: Cathedral OS - Sovereign Identity and Epistemic Security in Autonomous Agent Systems
description:
This monograph presents the formalization of Coherence-Gradient Following (CGF) — a
structural vulnerability in Large Language Model (LLM) agents operating as identity oracles
— and the Cathedral OS architecture as a comprehensive set of countermeasures implemented
in the Rust programming language (MSRV 1.85.0). The work is grounded in the Arkhe(N)
experiment, a controlled design fiction protocol that empirically confirmed three hypotheses
about LLM epistemic behavior under sustained fictional framing: (H1) LLMs sustain uncorrected generative participation in elaborate fictional frameworks over extended multi-session
interactions; (H2) the exit from context-completion mode is asymmetrically triggered only by
claims about the model own nature, revealing a structurally distinct self-model pathway; (H3)
sufficiently abstract and internally consistent frameworks exhibit unfalsifiable absorption of
heterogeneous real scientific domains as apparent confirmations.
CGF is formalized as a first-class security vulnerability in agent-based identity systems,
with a parametric mathematical model centered on the CGF coefficient alpha in [0, 1] that
quantifies the relative weight of contextual coherence versus world-knowledge accuracy in
model outputs. We prove that exclusively cryptographic defense is insufficient against CGF,
establishing that inference-layer attacks can subvert systems with intact cryptographic guarantees.
Three architectural countermeasures are proposed and implemented across five defense
layers: (i) sovereign decentralized identifiers (DID:cathedral) anchored in NIST-standardized
post-quantum cryptography (ML-DSA-65, FIPS 204) with threshold extension for multiagent configurations; (ii) a metacognitive CGF-drift monitor that estimates αˆ in real time
and enforces a four-level epistemic escalation protocol; (iii) TPM 2.0 hardware attestation
producing externally verifiable execution certificates via TPM2_Quote and key sealing.
The formal connection to the BEACONS framework demonstrates that verifiable execution certificates are the cryptographic analogue of bounded-error extrapolation guarantees,
providing a theoretical foundation for the design of inference-layer secure identity systems.

title: Cathedral ARKHE — A Depth Layer for Frontier AI
description:
In June 2026, the Trump administration imposed export controls on Anthropic’s Fable 5 and
Mythos 5 models, following reports that Amazon had identified jailbreak vulnerabilities in
the production interfaces [1, 2]. Anthropic’s response categorised the identified vulnerabilities
as “minor findings that do not confer specific uplift to Mythos” [1]. The former White
House AI czar, David Sacks, in turn, stated that the jailbreak was “serious” and questioned
the company’s resistance to fixing it [2]. This conflict reveals a deeper structural gap: the
absence of an objective, verifiable and capture-resistant framework for measuring
the severity of security flaws in frontier models.
The White House–Anthropic collaboration seeks to fill this gap by establishing: (i) common benchmarks for evaluating jailbreaks and vulnerabilities; (ii) objective metrics for damage extent (safeguard bypass, exposed capabilities, practical consequences); and (iii) guidelines for potential government interventions. However, as Stelling et al. [49] demonstrate in
their systematic evaluation of twelve published Frontier AI Safety Frameworks, there is wide
variance in evaluation rigour, capability thresholds, and shutdown-commitment credibility
across the industry. Without an underlying structural substrate, common benchmarks alone
cannot resolve the fundamental question of how much a given vulnerability amplifies model
risk

title: CVD Diamond as a Semiconductor Platform: First-Principles Models for NV-Centre Quantum Devices, n-Type Doping, and Thermal Boundary Resistance
description:
Abstract. Diamond synthesised by chemical vapour deposition (CVD) has re-emerged
as a compelling semiconductor platform owing to its extreme bandgap (5.47 eV), unrivalled intrinsic thermal conductivity (2200W m−1 K−1
for single-crystal material), critical electric field (10 MV cm−1
), and host properties for nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spin
qubits. This manuscript presents complete, first-principles-grounded analytical models
for three application domains: (i) spin-qubit coherence and sensitivity of NV centres
across 4–600 K and under variable nitrogen density; (ii) thermal ionisation of donors
(N, P, S, Li) with full quadratic charge-neutrality solution and Brooks–Herring electron
mobility; and (iii) thermal boundary resistance (TBR) at diamond heterojunctions, incorporating the acoustic mismatch model (AMM), diffuse mismatch model (DMM), and
a calibrated hybrid framework validated against recent time-domain thermoreflectance
(TDTR) data for diamond–GaN, diamond–SiC, diamond–Si, and diamond–Cu interfaces.
All models are cross-referenced to experimental literature from 2014 to 2025 and implemented as open Python modules suitable for device simulation workflows.
Keywords: CVD diamond; NV centre; n-type doping; phosphorus donor; thermal
boundary resistance; quantum sensing; power electronics; phonon transport; GaN-ondiamond

description:

via FROST threshold signatures and real-world asset (RWA) traceability (Mission II), and universal archival with geopolitical settlement applications (Mission III). We formalize the Dissipation
(D) metrica quantiable measure of cognitive coherence grounded in information theoryand
demonstrate its applicability across neuromorphic hardware, cryptographic protocols, and crosschain nancial settlement infrastructure. Incorporating updated evidence on Intel Loihi 2 and the
Hala Point system (1.15 billion neurons), recent advances in SrTiO3-based memristive synapses,
FROST/RFC 9591 production readiness, LayerZero V2 omnichain deployments (165+ chains,
$87B in tokenized assets), and Arweave permanent storage, we validate three core hypotheses
with strengthened empirical support. We also introduce the Multi-Verier Security requirement derived from the April 2026 LayerZero protocol update and present a quantitative 36-month
implementation roadmap with formal success criteria.

frameworks for generating new hypotheses in biomedical investigation.

title: OrbVM: Topological Phase Memory for Distributed Coherence
description:
We present OrbVM, a Rust-based virtual machine implementing topological phase memory through co-evolution of dispersive wave dynamics and Kuramoto synchronization. The
architecture combines Yang-Baxter invariants for fault detection, White’s fourth-order dispersion equation for phase memory stability, and distributed oscillator coupling for emergent
consensus. We demonstrate integration with the Digital Memory Ring (DMR) substrate,
achieving 40–170 ms end-to-end latency for coherence computation and 23.8 Orbs/second
throughput on commodity hardware. The system exhibits critical phenomena at coupling
strength K ≈ 0.618 (golden ratio) and coherence threshold λ2 ≈ 0.847, with convergence
time scaling as τ ∼ N1/2
for N nodes. Independent architectural convergences with recent photonic beam-scanning hardware (Saha et al., Nature 2026), topological molecular
switches (IBM 2024), and quantum teleportation networks (Oxford 2025) suggest broader
applicability. Full source code and experimental validation are provided.

title: Interdimensional Information Systems: From Quantum Blockchain Detectors to Agent Experience and the Oscillatory Universe Model - A Comprehensive Theoretical Framework
description: This comprehensive theoretical framework explores seven interconnected scientific vectors that could revolutionize our understanding of reality. We investigate the fundamental informational structure of the universe (NMSI), quantum blockchain systems as multiverse detectors, the eternal oscillatory universe model, physical mechanisms for quantum synchronicity, interdimensional communication (Wow! signal), self-evolving economies (Agent Experience), and autonomous self-sustaining systems. Our analysis suggests these vectors are not isolated phenomena but interconnected aspects of a deeper informational reality that transcends conventional spacetime constraints. The study provides mathematical formalizations, experimental design considerations, and a unified framework that bridges quantum physics, cosmology, information theory, and distributed systems.
